content:
maria: quick heads-up — spotted ~15% microbatch throughput drop on canary-3 (us-west) around 02:12 UTC, 95p latency +40ms. no obvious error spikes in logs. pinging owners @kevin @olga
kevin: thanks. can you paste the canary id and a link to the dashboard?
mar ia: oops typo — canary id is canary-3B. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/canaries/canary-3B
jaspreet: saw the alert too. did we roll any kernel bits or scheduler changes yesterday evening?
kevin: only the small microbatch PR merged — PR #5421 (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5421). it touched continuous-batching window calculation.
simon: FYI that PR adjusted target_batch_ms from 12 -> 10 for small requests; expected higher throughput but maybe edge effects.
olga: can we get a quick flame/alloc profile for a slow request? i want to rule out more frequent cache misses in KV layer.
maria: grabbing traces now, will paste snippet.
ci-bot: deploy-event: canary-3B rollout completed by kevin at 2026-03-18T01:58:41Z (sha: a1b2c3d) :robot_face:
kevin: ok thanks. @maria if traces show KV miss rate up, that points to warmup/eviction interaction with shorter batch windows.
maria: trace top lines:
```
latency_ms: 320
kv_miss_rate: 0.23
batch_size_avg: 1.8
cpu_user: 42%
```
jaspreet: miss_rate 23% is up from baseline 8% — that's significant. were there concurrent cache evictions?
olga: check cache-evict logs around 02:05-02:15 — possible housekeeping job kicked in.
simon: i pulled the eviction logs: we had a background compaction job on node group n-west-5 at 02:09, TTL purge removed ~12k entries.
kevin: aha — compaction + smaller batch window = more cold starts and smaller K/V reuse. that could explain throughput drop.
maria: agree. mitigation idea: bump target_batch_ms back to 12 for canary-3B and schedule compaction off-peak.
jaspreet: @kevin can you open a rollback or hotfix PR? small change + canary patch preferred.
kevin: i'll open PR #5430 to revert the target_batch_ms change for canary rollouts. linking: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5430
olga: also adding a temp rule to defer compaction if canary traffic > 40rps. filing ops ticket.
simon: ops ticket created: OPS-2298. I'll tag infra to pick a better compaction window.
maria: timeline? can we get hotfix out in next 30m?
kevin: aiming for PR, CI run, and canary by +25m. will post status.
maria: thanks — once canary stabilizes please post delta on 50/95p and batch_size_avg.
kevin: PR merged and canary redeploy started at 02:34 UTC. monitoring.
ci-bot: canary-rollout: canary-3B redeploy started (sha: d4e5f6)
maria: early numbers: 95p latency back down ~ -35ms vs peak, batch_size_avg up to 2.1, kv_miss_rate down to 10%.
jaspreet: looks good. postmortem/notes: avoid compaction during microbatch-sensitive rollouts; add a heuristic in compaction to defer when avg_batch_size < 2.5.
kevin: filing small follow-ups: runtime PR to add compaction-defer flag, and a config tweak for autoscaler to prefer slightly larger batch windows under high KV-eviction churn.
olga: i'll add a quick perf test to the canary checklist to catch KV miss regressions (script link: https://git.internal/redwood/tests/perf/canary_kv_check).
maria: awesome. thanks all for fast responses. marking resolved for now but leaving OPS-2298 open until postmortem is written.
simon: adding action items: KEVIN -> PR #5430 (done), KEVIN -> follow-up runtime PR, OLGA -> perf test, SIMON -> infra compaction window tweak, MARIA -> assemble postmortem draft.
maria: pinging @everyone: please ack if you own any of the action items above or need me to reassign. :thumbsup:
kevin: ack (owned PRs)
j aspreet: ack (monitoring + canary watch)
olga: ack (perf test)
simon: ack (infra)
